provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 110-113; antecedent 1862 text-layer lines 21033-21038; 1922 Mame printed p. 89, artifact PDF p. 203
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1962 prints the conclusion written out (14 words); the public-domain witnesses abbreviate it to the short cue; 1862 text layer damages 6 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: deuotionem -> deuoti nem; quesumus -> que sumus; benignus -> beirignus; abstinentiam macerantur -> abstin n tiam macerdntur; corpore -> c rpore; operis reficiantur -> peris refi eiantur; 1922 Mame text layer damages 3 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): deuotionem -> euotionem; (nothing) -> d; operis -> peris; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 89, artifact PDF p. 203; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 27650 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Devotionem populi tui, quaesumus, Domine, benignus intende: ut, qui per
abstinentiam macerantur in corpore, per fructum boni operis reficiantur in
mente. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et
regnat in unitate.

propers.incipit: Custodi me, Domine, ut pupillam oculi
propers.name: Gradual

provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 115-116; antecedent 1862 text-layer lines 21143-21146; 1922 Mame printed p. 90, artifact PDF p. 204
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 conclusion is the shorter cue without nostrum; 1862 text layer damages 2 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: sacrificia domine quesumus propensius -> mine qusesu mus propitius; medicinalibus -> medicin libus; 1922 Mame text layer damages 3 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): sacrificia -> acrificia; quesumus -> que s sumus; nos -> hos; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 90, artifact PDF p. 204; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 27754 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer. Recorded limitation: The day was identified by the facsimile's own running head (Feria V post dominicam I in Quadragesima) and by the station heading that opens the formulary, and this oration is the first Secreta the Missal prints inside that day's Mass, taken after that day's Ant. ad Introitum and before the next day's station heading; the marginal number was read on the page image. Every 1862 reading in this entry rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone - this repository holds no page images for its temporal run - so where that layer damages a word the letterforms are inferred from the 1922 Mame at the same place rather than read. The 1922 Mame's text layer is also noisy here (0.83); its reading was accepted where the 1862 and the 1962 target agree with it. Not checked: the Oratio super populum that the 1962 prints after this Mass's Postcommunion (not on this work list), the 1604 and the 1570, and whether the 1862 also prints this prayer elsewhere in its book.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Sacrificia, Domine, quaesumus, propensius ista nos salvent, quae
medicinalibus sunt instituta jejuniis. Per Dominum nostrum.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Tuorum nos, Domine, largitate donorum, et temporalibus attolle praesidiis,
et renova sempiternis. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui
tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.
